standard.title: Create Descriptions and Explanations
standard.description: create descriptions and explanations, using economic and business knowledge, concepts and terms, and referencing information and data from sources
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can present descriptions and explanations drawing on findings and viewpoints from sources using relevant terms and conventions (AC9HS6S07). The Year 7 demand adds domain-specific economic vocabulary — market, income, business, goods and services, costs and benefits — and requires students to embed data and information from sources explicitly in their explanations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create descriptions and explanations, using economic and business knowledge, concepts and terms, and referencing information and data from sources.

nodes.label: Orienting an audience to an economic issue
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop the opening of a response that orients the audience to an economic issue using relevant economic concepts and terms.
nodes.minimum_width: Write an opening paragraph that names the issue, identifies the audience, and uses at least two economic terms accurately.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a response opening that orients the audience (peers or community members) to the economic issue — introducing the issue, explaining its relevance, and using economic and business concepts and terms such as market, income, business, goods and services, costs and benefits accurately and purposefully.
wider: Adapt the same economic issue explanation for two different audiences — for example, a Year 7 peer and an adult community member — comparing how vocabulary, detail level and framing shift
Evaluate a sample economic explanation for audience orientation: does it establish the issue clearly? Does the vocabulary suit the audience? What would improve it?
Develop an orientation for an economic issue affecting a specific community (e.g. a First Nations regional community) where the audience is community members rather than students
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot orient their audience to the issue will produce explanations that assume shared context and vocabulary, making their work inaccessible and communicatively ineffective. The orientation is also the point at which economic vocabulary is established — failures here cascade into imprecise use throughout the explanation.

response_modes.reason: Students need explicit scaffolding for how to open an economic explanation: name the issue, state why it matters, define any specialist terms the audience may not know, then proceed to the argument. Model this structure before students apply it independently.

success_criteria: Writes an opening that names the economic issue and its relevance to the audience
Uses at least two economic or business terms accurately in the opening

nodes.label: Explaining with data and appropriate formats
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain ideas and decisions with details and examples, using data and information presented in appropriate formats — visual displays, tables, graphs, budget and savings plans.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain one idea or decision using at least one piece of data or information from a source, presented in an appropriate format (table, graph, or visual display).
nodes.typical_width: Explain ideas and decisions with details and examples, using data and information presented in appropriate formats — visual displays, tables, graphs, budget and savings plans, research findings in graphic organisers or summaries; select the format that best supports the explanation for the intended audience.
wider: Produce an explanation that integrates multiple data formats — for example, a written explanation supported by a graph and a budget plan — and evaluate which format added most value
Develop an explanation in a multi-modal format (e.g. a short presentation or infographic) that combines written explanation with data visualisation, targeting a specific audience

Create an explanation of an economic issue facing a First Nations community that draws on community-sourced data or reports, presenting the data in a format that respects and centres community context

response_modes.reason: Students need practice with multiple formats before they can select the most appropriate one for a given audience and explanation type. Provide structured opportunities to use each format type — table, graph, budget, visual display — and have students reflect on which worked best for their explanation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of formats — visual displays, tables, graphs, budget plans, graphic organisers — and the range of audiences and issues to which they can be applied creates genuine width in the communication dimension of this skill. Students who practise across more formats and contexts develop a transferable and flexible communication repertoire.
success_criteria: Explains an idea or decision using at least one piece of referenced data or information
Presents data or information in a format appropriate to the explanation and audience
Uses economic and business terms (market, income, goods and services, costs and benefits) accurately throughout
